stops.text: His family begins every good thing with Ganesha. This one was painted in Mithila, in Bihar.
Her family follows the Buddha’s path. At Ajanta, near her home, devotees bring lotuses.
Two blessings, side by side: may every good thing be yours.
His Bihar: at Chhath, women stand in the river and raise baskets of fruit to the sun.
Her Maharashtra: in Paithan, home of the Paithani, painters showed two mothers embracing.
Old threads already join them: the very name Bihar comes from vihara, a Buddhist monastery.
Turmeric at a Patna market. In Bihar, married women bless the couple with it, and with rice.
At Ajanta, in her Maharashtra, women bathe a king of Mithila before his great day.
In Maharashtra the turmeric touches him first; what is left, the ushti halad, goes to her.
Patna, around 1795: a dhol, a daf and colour in the air. Bihar celebrates out loud.
In Pune they play fugdi: two women cross hands, lean back and spin.
A nine-yard sari, a pearl nath, green bangles: dressed for a Marathi celebration.
Women on both sides sang as they worked, jatsar in Bihar and ovi in Maharashtra. Tonight, everyone sings.
His side arrives at night: torches, a band, and the groom in his palanquin.
Paithan, around 1850: a bride bows, and the women of her family bless her.
Rice from his side, petals from hers: the blessings fall on both of them together.
